Whoever [Col. 1268D] among free persons, for the salvation of his or her soul, has bound himself or herself to serve God at your monastery, or in its chapels or dependent places, by vow and by the title of profession according to the institution of Robert the priest of blessed memory, shall by no means have licence to abandon that place and transfer to another without the common consent of the convent.

Moreover, no one whatsoever may occupy or presumptuously harass chapels that have been built by you with episcopal permission, or that shall hereafter be built. Certainly, those assigned to divine service in your chapels shall have free burial there. Furthermore, let no one presume to demand from you tithes of your animals or of crops cultivated at your own expense.

We decree [Col. 1269A] that whatever goods or possessions the same monastery now lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s grant, through the concession of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the generosity of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and to those who succeed you, saving the right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make fitting amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his or her power and office; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; and let him or her be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus [Col. 1269B] Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for the same monastery may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of November, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1126 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

## L. To Didacus, Archbishop of Compostela. (Year 1126.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XX, 445.]

[Col. 1269C]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother DIDACUS, Archbishop of Compostela, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The noble and renowned Church of Compostela is honoured by religious men and lovers of the Christian name because of reverence for the blessed Apostle James. Since, therefore, it has pleased divine providence to summon you to govern so great a Church, we exhort your brotherhood in the Lord to conduct yourself wisely, gently, and humbly, and to carry out what must be done, so that you may deserve to become pleasing to God, to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, and to the people entrusted to you. We have received your letters and messengers with paternal charity. As to what answer we should give [Col. 1269D] to your petitions, we have not yet taken counsel.

## LI. To Adelbert, Archbishop of Mainz. (Between 1125 and 1127.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 351.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., Archbishop of Mainz, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Concerning the case of Gebhard, about whom your brotherhood asked us, we sought the counsel of our brethren, the bishops and cardinals. By their deliberation it has been determined that the same Gebhard ought no longer to retain the summit of the episcopate in the Church of Würzburg [Herbipolis]. [Col. 1270A]

Given at the Lateran, the fourth day before the Nones of March.

## LII. To the Canons of St Fridianus at Lucca. (Between 1125 and 1127, 17 May.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Lucchese edition, IV, 588.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., prior, and the brethren of St Fridianus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as things irrationally done ought on no account to endure, so things canonically determined ought to remain with firm stability. We therefore ratify, and command that it be observed without contradiction, the unanimous judgment issued by our venerable brother B., bishop of Lucca, between you and the hospital of Altopascio [Col. 1270B] concerning the wood on the hill of Sacco.

Given at the Lateran, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June.

## LIII. He confirms the discipline, possessions, and privileges of the monastery of St Ulrich and St Afra at Kreuzlingen. (Between 1125 and 1127.)

[NEUGART, *Codex diplomaticus Alemannicus*, II, 60.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ HENRY, provost, and the brethren professing the regular life in the hospital and church of St Ulrich the Confessor and St Afra the Martyr, both present and future, for ever.

[Note: [Col. 1269D] Namely, at Kreuzlingen; the church of that community of Augustinian regular canons, outside the walls of the city of Constance, is dedicated in memory of those same saints [Col. 1270D].]

Both the affection of fraternal charity and the devotion of a pious [Col. 1270C] will persuade us to grant the petitions of religious brethren. Therefore, graciously assenting to the requests brought before us by our beloved and venerable brother UDALRIC, bishop of Constance, we decree that the order of canonical life which he established in your church and hospice according to the Rule of St Augustine shall be preserved inviolate in future times.

We confirm by this present decree the benefices which he granted you from the episcopal table—yet for the greater part from his other goods—for the support of the common sustenance and the refreshment of Christ’s poor. We further confirm the exchange which you made with the canons of the greater church of St Mary of Constance and with the canons of St Stephen, with the assent and approval of the same bishop.

[Note: [Col. 1270D] The church of St Stephen, the first after the cathedral church of Constance.]

Whatever you now lawfully possess through the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other means, or may hereafter justly and canonically acquire through God’s bounty, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; rather, let all be preserved whole for the uses of the clergy and the poor, to their complete benefit, while in all things the reverence due to the bishop of Constance is preserved. [Col. 1271A]

When the provost of your church dies, let all the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God, provide for themselves a suitable person to be canonically elected. We likewise decree that the burial-place of that location shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make fitting amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; and let him or her be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God [Col. 1271B] and of our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

## LIV. He rebukes A[delbert], Archbishop of Mainz, because, before the case had been adjudicated, he excommunicated contrary to the canons the bishop-designate of the Church of Würzburg. (Between 1126 and 1127.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 349.]

H., servant of God, to his venerable brother A., Archbishop of Mainz and legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and [Col. 1271C] apostolic blessing.

We know indeed that you have zeal for God; yet, without prejudice to charity, you ought to temper it, so that you may do nothing indiscreetly, but may do all things reasonably and according to God. For the bishop-designate of the Church of Würzburg lodged before us complaints that he is oppressed by you contrary to justice and suffers prejudice, because you deprived him of ecclesiastical communion as an invader of the Church in which he asserts that he was elected, and pronounced him a simoniac, although he had been convicted neither by accusers nor lawful witnesses, had not voluntarily confessed, and had not been canonically examined.

If this is so, it is clear that your brotherhood has departed from the divinely inspired canonical rules. Sacred canonical authority therefore says [Col. 1271D] that a bishop must not be deprived of his bishopric before the outcome of his case is apparent. Again, from the letter of a pope written to Anastasius and the other bishops assembled in the Alexandrian synod:

> “Concerning the trials of bishops, on which you consulted us, we find diverse rules established by the Fathers. Some commanded that a year and six months be granted, in order to repel the schemes of accusers, prepare their own replies, establish witnesses, and seek councils of bishops; others, with whom the greater number agree, [commanded] a year.”

Yet I find no period shorter than six months; and since these allowances were granted to laymen, how much more to priests? For postponements ought to be granted not within a narrow time but over a long interval, so that the accused may prepare themselves [Col. 1272A] and fully arm themselves against plotters. Judges and accusers, moreover, ought to be persons free from every suspicion, who desire to pronounce their judgment from the root of charity.

## LV. To Peter, Abbot of Cluny.—On the death and burial of the invader Pontius. (Year 1127.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 321.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

In the past month of December Pontius entered upon the way of all flesh. Although, often warned to do penance for the evils inflicted upon Cluny, he refused, [Col. 1272B] nevertheless, out of reverence for that monastery, of which he had been a monk, we caused him to be honourably buried.

Given at the Lateran.

## LVI. He forbids Pandulf, son of Count Landulf of Aquino, to build a castle on the possession of St Peter. (Year 1127.)

[See PETER, *Chronicle of Monte Cassino*, book IV, chapter 93.]

## LVII. He informs bishops, abbots, barons, and others established throughout England that he has entrusted William, Archbishop of Canterbury, with the legation of England and Scotland. (Year 1127, 25 January.)

[WHARTON, *Anglia sacra*, I, 729.]

[Col. 1272C]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brothers and sons—the bishops, abbots, barons, and all other clergy and laity established throughout England and Scotland—greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Church, bride of Christ, rooted in the firmament of apostolic faith, is accustomed, like a devoted and gracious mother, to provide the nourishment of life for her gentle and humble children, both those who are far away and those who are near. Those near at hand are visited through the presence shown them by our own person; those far away, through the ministry of our legates. Since, therefore, we know you to be the unique and special sons of blessed Peter, we have entrusted our functions in England and Scotland to our dearest [Col. 1272D] brother William, Archbishop of Canterbury, so that, appointed there by us as legate of the Apostolic See and supported by the help of your charity, he may, with the Lord at work, correct what requires correction and strengthen what requires strengthening, to the honour of God and the holy Roman Church and for the salvation of your souls.

Therefore, commanding, we direct all of you humbly to obey him as our legate; and, whenever you are summoned by him for the condition of the Churches and the increase of Christian religion, unanimously to assemble at his call and diligently celebrate synodal assemblies with him.

Given at the Lateran, the eighth day before the Kalends of February.

## LVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St Peter at Chartres, concerning the several churches confirmed to it. (Year 1127, 8 March.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, VIII, 325.]

[Col. 1273A]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ WILLIAM, abbot of the monastery of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, situated in the suburb of the city of Chartres, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

The principle of equity and justice persuades us to grant churches enduring security of their property and records of unshaken force. For it is not fitting that Christ’s servants, devoted to divine service, should be harassed by the perverse molestations of wicked people and wearied by the rash [Col. 1273B] vexations of anyone whatsoever; likewise, estates dedicated to the uses of heavenly mysteries ought to endure no exactions of the powerful and nothing extraordinary.

Accordingly, prompted by this consideration of charity, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot William, and inclined by the prayers of our venerable brother Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, we assent to your reasonable petitions and protect by the page of this present writing our monastery of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, established in the suburb of Chartres and ruled by you under God. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and lawfully holds through the grant of the bishops of Chartres, the liberality of kings, the generosity of princes, and the offerings of the faithful, or may hereafter acquire by God’s bounty through just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have judged the following worthy of express naming:

The church of St Germanus of Alogia, with the chapel of Domna Petra; the church of St Leobinus of Braiacum; the church of St Peter of Arro with its chapels; the church of St Mary of Evorea; the church of Villaevillonis; the church of St Mary of Stelliones; the church of Luigniacum; the church of Domna Petra; the church of St Leobinus of Châteaudun; the church of St Stephen of Spelterol; the church of Tornesiacum; the church of the chapel of Osana; the church of Verrigniacum; the church of Billoncellis; the church of Sonnenchiis; the church of Puteosa with its chapel; the church of Mansellaria; [Col. 1273D] the church of Resuntis; the church of Morivillare; the church of Mutionisvillare; the church of Capella Fortini; the church of Rivellonium; the church of Fursonisvillare; the church of Vitraicum; the church of Belchia; the church of Rudetum; the church of Alnetum; the church of Monasteriolum; the church of St Martin of Firmericuria; the church of Nantilliacum; the church of Olins; the church of Anetum; the church of Salectum; the church of St Mary of Moncelli, with the chapel of Sorel; the church of Chalgetum; the church of Vi; and the revenue of the prebend of the church of St Martin in Valle.

In the diocese of Orléans: the church of St Paternus; and the church of Niz. In the diocese of Évreux: the church of Bellolocus; the church of St Christopher; [Col. 1274A] the church of Canziacum; the church of Illeiis; the church of St George; and the church of Purlaicum. In the diocese of Sées: the church of Planches; the church of St Lawrence; and the church of Brogilo Amaro. In the diocese of Rouen: the church of Leoniscuria; the church of Guerriacum; the church of Aldoenivilla; and the church of Gundelicuria. Moreover, in the aforesaid diocese of Chartres: the church of Treione; the church of St Germanus of Guastina; and the church of Isis.

These three last-mentioned churches shall remain in their freedom, exempt from every exaction and payment of synod and *circada*, without prejudice to episcopal right. We therefore decree, etc. I, Honorius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1274B] Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1127 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

## LIX. Bull, or diploma, confirming the foundation of the abbey of Sponheim. Year 1127, 23 March.

[*Gallia Christiana*, V, 448.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERNHELM, abbot of the monastery of St Martin at Sponheim, of the Order of St Benedict in the diocese of Mainz, and to his successors canonically instituted for ever.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires. Therefore, beloved son, assenting to the just petitions of you and your brethren, we receive the aforesaid monastery of Sponheim, over which you preside by God’s appointment, under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and have fortified it by the page of this present writing. We decree and ordain that the regular life newly established in that place according to the Rule of St Benedict shall be preserved inviolate in future times.

Moreover, after making profession among you, no one may transfer to another place without the abbot’s licence, under pretext of a stricter or more relaxed religious life. Should anyone hereafter depart contrary to this our prohibition, no abbot or other person may dare to retain him. Whenever, upon the death of an abbot, the brethren [Col. 1274D] of that place must deliberate concerning his successor, no person shall be imposed there by any artifice of fraud or by force of any power, ecclesiastical or temporal, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of St Benedict, judge ought to be elected from the same community, or from another if—God forbid—they cannot find a suitable person among themselves.

The consecration of altars, chrism, holy oil, blessing of abbots, and ordination of monks shall be received from the diocesan archbishop of that district, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these freely and without any improper demand. Otherwise, it shall be lawful for you and your successors to approach whatever Catholic bishop you choose and receive consecrations and sacraments from him. [Col. 1275A]

We also decree that the burial-place of this monastery shall be wholly free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and will of those who desire to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated. We confirm by apostolic authority all possessions which you hold by just title and may hereafter acquire through anyone’s offering. We decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain in any manner what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, let all be preserved whole for the benefit of you and the poor.

But if any archbishop, bishop, king, duke, count, [Col. 1275B] prince of any rank, or any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and does not immediately make fitting amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and office; let him or her know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him or her be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of the Lord God, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him or her be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given through the hand of the deacon of the Holy Apostolic See, [Col. 1275C] on the tenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1127 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of our pontificate.

## LX. To Richard, Bishop of Bayeux—That he should no longer infringe the rights of the monastery of St Benignus at Dijon. (Year 1127, 6 May.)

[PÉRARD, *Recueil de pièces pour servir à l'histoire de Bourgogne*, p. 219.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to RICHARD, bishop of Bayeux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Among the many complaints deserving correction which we have heard concerning your brotherhood, the cry of the Church of Dijon has come forward to increase our indignation. I cannot fail to hear it, because it has always been venerable to our predecessors, and because it pleads both the merit of its religious life and a certain privilege arising from its ancient affection toward us. It complains, indeed, that you transgress and shift its boundaries, annul its old and ancient cemetery by means of a new cemetery, draw priests subject to its jurisdiction into your jurisdiction contrary to right, demand from them synodal, customary, and even extraordinary payments, and do many things of this kind which plainly appear to protest against justice. [Col. 1276A]

Therefore, in order to establish the truth, we ordered the charters and decretals on which it seemed to rely to be produced. While we were engaged in reading them, weighty and trustworthy persons rose from our side and said that they had heard and seen when the bishop of Bayeux gave to the monks of Dijon the gift signified in the document: first in Auvergne, then at Rome, through the hand of Pope Urban, with complete freedom and without any exception except obedience alone, which is universally owed to every pontifical authority. I myself remember seeing this when at that time I was in the service of that most blessed pope.

Since these things are so, and the matter has not yet passed from memory because it occurred recently, and what was done is still attested by many surviving and competent witnesses, and what has been attested is confirmed by apostolic documents, I wonder by what rashness you have dared to infringe so solemn a right, even in a small matter. Even if the authority of witnesses and documents were absent, it could nevertheless easily be inferred from the man’s innate greatness [Col. 1276B] that he took away nothing from so celebrated and devout a gift as could have been granted. For he knew that almsgiving benefits the giver more than the recipient.

If, therefore, reason could instruct you, being prudent, toward a work of piety; if the pious memory of so great a shepherd could move you, being pious; if the downfall of your predecessor Thorold, in this very matter and for a just cause, could make you fearful: since you do not fear to exceed so many bounds of equity, it is ours to correct what you exceed. Accordingly, by the authority available to us we confirm to the monks of Dijon the monastery of St Vigor with its appurtenances, and everything contained in the charter of the pope and of Robert, duke of Normandy, as our holy Fathers Urban, Paschal, and Calixtus did, with the full freedom of all their property. Thus they themselves, their churches, their priests, and everything subject to their right shall be wholly remote from any payment, exaction, legal action—whether just or unjust—by you or your successors; but whatever it may be shall remain entirely under the right and discretion of the monks. [Col. 1276C]

For what has once been given to the Church is wholly removed from the giver’s control; no one may reclaim what he has given, and, if this is done, it is sacrilege. Likewise, according to the decree of Hormisdas, no bishop may forbid divine office in their monasteries, so long as they are known to be in communion with the Apostolic See.

We strengthen the monks’ established position in such a way that we do not wish to abolish your honour; rather, we set limits so that they may show you the service of sincere affection, while you provide them patronage freely, not for hire. Let there be between you a contest of goodwill, not an auction for any price. For he who first admitted them as friends was able to ensure that they were not tributaries to him, and to become himself the sweet father of sons, not the auctioneer of strangers. [Col. 1276D]

If anyone knowingly transgresses the boundary of this decree, unless he comes to his senses, let him be anathema. If any of the canons causes himself to be buried anywhere other than in the appointed cemetery of blessed Vigor, both the buried person and the person who buries him shall become guilty of transgression; let them see to it. But upon everyone obedient and cooperative may there be both our blessing and an eternal dwelling in heaven.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Nones of May, through the hand of Imericus, deacon-cardinal of the Holy Roman [Col. 1277A] Church, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1127 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

## LXI. To Otto, Bishop of Halberstadt. (Year 1127, 18 October.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 477.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Halberstadt, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A grave complaint concerning your person has reached us. We have learned that you occupied the bishopric of Halberstadt by lay violence and, what is more detestable, through the simoniacal heresy. How greatly the holy Church of God abhors this foul plague of simoniacal [Col. 1277B] heresy is shown by the Apostle Peter at the beginning of the nascent Church, when he condemned Simon, who wished to sell the Holy Spirit, together with his money. If, therefore, you know yourself guilty of this crime, it is better to yield and punish your sin in this life through penance than to appear for judgment before the eyes of the strict Judge.

Given at B., on the tenth day before the Kalends of November.

## LXII. He confirms the possessions of the Canons of Faenza. (Year 1128, 4 April.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, II, 494.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Faenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1277C] The pious solicitude of the pastoral office obliges us to grant the guardianship of the Apostolic See and the aid of protection to those who seek it. Therefore, dearest sons in Christ, canons of the Church of Faenza, assenting to your petitions, we receive both you yourselves and all your goods into the guardianship of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify you by the page of this present privilege. We decree that all goods which you now hold through the grant of any person, or may hereafter be able to acquire in any manner recognized by divine and human laws, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you.

We decree, therefore, that no archbishop, bishop, duke, margrave, count, viscount, castaldus, or any other person, great or small, of whatever rank or dignity, may dare to disturb you or anything you possess, take it away, retain what has been taken, diminish it, or harass you with any vexations. Rather, let all be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose sustenance and governance they were granted. If, however, you perceive that you are oppressed on any ground by any of the aforesaid persons, you may freely appeal to the Apostolic See. [Col. 1277D]

If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make fitting amends by adequate satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and rank, and know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed. But whoever proves a guardian and observer shall be filled with the grace of apostolic blessing and rejoice in the reward of eternal blessedness. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Honorius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, chancellor of the Holy Roman See and of the universal curia, on the day before the Nones of April, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1128 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

## LXIII. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Trier, and grants Archbishop Mainero the use of the pallium and a processional cross, and that “at the appointed stations of the Church he may ride with a white *nacco*.” (Year 1127, 9 April.) [Col. 1278B]

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 200.]

## LXIV. At the request of Bishop Dodo, he confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Modena and the possessions of its Church. (Year 1128, 27 April.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memorie storiche Modenesi*, Modena, 1793, quarto, II, 99.]

## LXV. To Matthew, Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See—On behalf of the monastery of Luxeuil, that property taken from it by the monks of Dijon be restored. (Year 1128, 4 May.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 266.]

[Col. 1278C]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother M[ATTHEW], bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Let the prudence of your brotherhood observe that the monastery of Luxeuil, through the acts of the monks of Dijon, has, as we have learned, been wearied by many oppressions from the times of our predecessors, namely the apostolic men Urban and Paschal. Pope Paschal of most blessed memory [Col. 1278D] himself commanded through apostolic letters that the men of Dijon should restore to the men of Luxeuil what had been taken from them. Yet this has not hitherto been carried into effect.

We therefore direct your experience, once the matter has been carefully examined, to invest the monastery of Luxeuil, according to the tenor of Pope Paschal of blessed memory, in what was taken from it, saving the right of the monastery of Dijon if it has any.

[Note: [Col. 1277D] The controversy concerned the cells of Clermont and Vangionis-rivus (Vignory). On this matter see the notice of the settlement made in 1129 in Pérard, p. 224, [Col. 1278D] and the letters of Wilencus, bishop of Langres, describing the course of events, ibid., p. 228.]

Moreover, let the men of Dijon, having summoned the men of Luxeuil, appear before us on the next feast of the Purification of Blessed Mary, so that they may maintain their right.

Given at the Lateran, the fourth day before the Nones of May.

## LXVI. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of St Fridianus at Lucca. (Year 1128, 7 May.)

[Col. 1279A]

[See the *Lateran Bullarium*, published at Rome in 1727, folio, p. 8.]

## LXVII. To the bishops of the province of Tours, that they observe the decrees of the Council of Nantes. (Year 1128, 20 May.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 354.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers, the suffragan bishops of the metropolitan see of Tours, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our dearest brother Hildebert, bishop of Tours, watching over his flock as a good shepherd, summoned his brethren and other religious men and, as we have learned by examining his letters, celebrated a council in the city of Nantes according to metropolitan custom. There, treating diligently of incestuous marriages, the illegitimate sons of priests, those who sought ecclesiastical benefices as though by hereditary succession, and other matters, he corrected what needed correction and established what needed establishment. We therefore direct all of you to observe without contradiction what is known to have been decreed there by him, in accordance with the decrees of the holy Fathers, for the honour of the Lord and the salvation of the people.

For just as in the structure of the human body the members serve and obey the head as their supreme guardian, so that the person may be preserved sound, so the minds of the faithful, made of one will, ought humbly to obey their prelates for the preservation of the unity of faith and the condition of the Church. [Col. 1279C]

Furthermore, we condemn those wicked customs renounced by the most illustrious count of Brittany into the hand of the aforesaid archbishop [alternative reading: “in the presence of the synod”]. One was that, when husbands or wives died, their movable goods were seized by secular authority. The other was that those who escaped shipwreck were deprived even of things afterwards found in port. By apostolic authority we forbid anyone to presume to revive them in future times.

For we judge it unjust that a person whom the greatness of divine mercy has rescued from the devouring violence of the raging [Col. 1279D] sea should be despoiled by the savage rapacity of men. The authority of pious emperors has provided that ownership is not lost even of goods thrown overboard in a storm to lighten a ship. No one casts them away because he does not wish to possess them, but in order to escape danger; and whoever takes the goods themselves with intent to profit commits theft.

Given at the Lateran, the thirteenth day before the Kalends of June.

## LXVIII. To Baldwin, King of Jerusalem. (Year 1128, 29 May.)

[Eugène de ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre de Jérusalem*, Paris, 1849, quarto, p. 17.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest [Col. 1280A] son in Christ BALDWIN, illustrious king of Jerusalem, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We render praises and thanksgivings to the Lord, author of all good things, who by the wondrous ordering of His providence has established you as king of Jerusalem. For from the reports of our brethren William, archbishop of Tyre, and Roger, bishop of Rheims—wise and prudent men, the envoys of your nobility—we have learned that you are both a cultivator of justice and a lover of religion; whence great joy has arisen in our heart. Supported by these two virtues, you preserve in royal peace and prudence what your predecessors, the glorious men Duke Godfrey and King Baldwin, won by the labours of war, [Col. 1280B] and you have manfully acquired many other things granted you from heaven through victory, amid very many hardships. For you have endured many dangers of death, the bitterness of wounds, the dreadful prisons of raging pagans, and even servile chains for the name of Christ, who, although equal to the Father, took the form of a servant. Therefore, casting your hope and confidence upon the Lord, whom no one has served without reward, persevere humbly in your good purpose. And we, who, though unworthy, sit in the chair of blessed Peter, love your person with true charity in the Lord; and by apostolic authority we grant to you the kingdom of Jerusalem with its dignity, finally granted by our predecessor Pope Paschal of blessed memory, with the measured discretion of justice, to your predecessor King Baldwin and to the Church of Jerusalem. [Col. 1280C] We command that the due honour of the kingdom and Church of Jerusalem be kept intact. Moreover, we earnestly commend to your prudence our most beloved son Fulk, count of Anjou, a vigorous and wise man, who, setting aside dominion over his barons and an innumerable people, and leaving the abundant richness of his own land, has resolved to serve God and you.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June [29 May].

LXIX. To the Tyrians.—He states that he has bestowed the pallium upon William, elected archbishop of Tyre and consecrated by the patriarch of Jerusalem. (1128.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 321.]

[Col. 1280D]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the suffragan bishops, clergy, and people of Tyre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We received with due charity our most beloved brother William, your archbishop, when he came to us. Having learned that he had been canonically elected and consecrated by our venerable brother Guarimund, patriarch of Jerusalem, we adorned him with the dignity of the pallium, that is, with the fullness of the pontifical office. Since, by the aid of divine mercy, we believe that his person will bring the greatest benefit to your mother Church of Tyre, we have thought fit to send him back to you with the favour of the Apostolic See and the support of our letters. Therefore, commanding your whole community, [Col. 1281A] we enjoin you graciously to receive him and humbly to render him submission, obedience, and reverence as your own metropolitan and bishop of your souls.

LXX. To Guarimund, archbishop of Jerusalem.—On the same matter. (1128.)

[Mansi, ibid.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Guarimund, patriarch of Jerusalem: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Having received the letters of your brotherhood, we graciously received our brother William, whom you consecrated archbishop in the Church of Tyre; and we adorned him with the dignity [Col. 1281B] of the pallium, namely, the fullness of the pontifical office. We have also commanded the suffragans of his church to render him submission and obedience as their own metropolitan.

Given in the territory of Bari, on the eighth day before the Ides of July [8 July].

LXXI. To Bernard, patriarch of Antioch, through Giles, bishop of Tusculum and legate of the Apostolic See: he commands him to restore to the Church of Tyre the suffragans whom he holds. (1128. Fragment.)

[WILLIAM of Tyre, bk. XIII, ch. 23.]

. . . . Therefore, by apostolic letters and through our venerable brother Giles, bishop of Tusculum, legate of the Apostolic See, we command you [Col. 1281C] to restore to the Church of Tyre its suffragans; and if, within forty days after inspection of the letters which we have sent to them, they do not render him due submission, then from that time we suspend them from the office of bishop.

LXXII. Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. (1128, 4 September.)

[Eug. de ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, p. 18.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons William, prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and his brethren professing the canonical life, both present and future, for ever.

Those who dwell in the house of the Lord, united in the sincerity of charity, preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. For the religion of a pure mind, strengthened by the indissoluble bond of divine love, bends the countenance of the most merciful Creator by unceasingly pouring forth pure prayers, so that earthly things may be joined and made one with heavenly things. For just as the inward spirit governs and gives life to the frame of the human body, so the graciousness of divine inspiration is the governing power of the vigour and salvation of the religious mind. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, canons of the glorious Sepulchre of the Lord, since we have learned that you are devoted to divine service and live religiously, and since, at the intervention also of our most beloved fellow-brother Guarmund, patriarch of Jerusalem, [Col. 1282A] we grant assent to your reasonable requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own protection your persons, possessions, and goods which you now justly and lawfully possess, or may in the future, through God’s bounty, acquire by lawful means; and we confirm them by the authority of this document. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

in the diocese of Jerusalem: the church of Saint Lazarus, with its castle and all its appurtenances; the castle of Maome, with its church and all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Caesarea in Palestine: the castle of Feniculi, with its church and all its appurtenances;

in the city of Jaffa: the church of Saint Peter, with all its appurtenances;

in the city of Tyre: the church of Saint Mary of the ancient [Col. 1282B] see, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Tripoli, in the castle of Mont Peregrin: the church of the Holy Sepulchre, with all its appurtenances;

in the same diocese: the church of Saint George, which is in the mountains, with all its appurtenances; likewise the village called Bivora, with all its appurtenances;

in Apulia, in the city of Brindisi: the church of the Holy Sepulchre and the church of Saint Lawrence, with all their appurtenances;

in the diocese of Embrun: the church of the Holy Sepulchre of Kayocas; the churches of the Holy Sepulchre, Saint Peter, and Saint Pontius of Sedena; the church of Saint John of Espinacis and the church of Saint Peter of Avanzo, with all their appurtenances;

in the diocese of Maguelonne: the church of Saint Saviour of Rubro, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Albi: the church of Saint Mary of Sepfacta, with all its appurtenances; also the village called Lugan; the holding called Cantol; the holdings Lubusreth and Dei; the holding Alaphenazem, with the church of [Saint] Mary and all its appurtenances; the holding Las Cruces of Saint Amarant; the holding Castandel; the holding Viarlar; the holding called Villa Godor; the church of Saint Osmerius, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Saintes: the church of Saint Peter of Macapzhana, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Bazas: the church of Saint Osbert, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Barcelona: the church of the Holy Sepulchre of Lathablatha, [Col. 1282D] with all its appurtenances;

in the same diocese, at Palma: the church of Saint Peter and the church of Saint John, with all their appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Patris;

in the diocese of Vic: the church of Saint Mary of Coseoliis, with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Andrew, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Urgell: one half of the castle of Mirabel, with its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Nájera: the church of Saint Mary of Gronio, with all its appurtenances; the hospice of Villa Rubea, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Burgos: the church of Saint Clement of Covas, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Michael of Quantana, with all its appurtenances;

in the castle of Sorizh: the church of Saint Andrew [Col. 1283A] and the church of Saint Marina, with all their appurtenances;

in the village called Clunia: the church of Saint Andrew, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Palencia: the church of Saint Mary of Pisorga, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Alexander of Valtanas, with all its appurtenances;

in the castle of Verde: the church of Saint Michael and the monastery of Saint Romanus, with all their appurtenances;

in the castle of Corel: the church of Saint Justus, the church of Saint Marina, and the church of Saint Eugratia, with all their appurtenances;

in the castle of Portel: the church of Saint Michael of Vega, with all its appurtenances;

near the city of Palencia: the church of Saint Emilian of Veruesca, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Pelagius of Valle [Col. 1283B] de Pero, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Sandronas, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Pilelas, with all its appurtenances;

in the village of Feles: the church of Saint Michael, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Segovia: the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Coca; the church of Saint Saviour; and the church of Saint Mary called Bovada, with all their appurtenances;

in the city of Ávila: the church of Saint Mary the New, with all its appurtenances;

at Arévalo: the church of Saint Peter in the old town, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Salamanca: the church of Saint Christopher, situated outside the city, with all its appurtenances;

at Medina: the church of the Holy Cross, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Zamora, in the castle called Toro: the church of the Holy Sepulchre, with all its appurtenances;

in the village of Lali: the church of Saint Eugenia, with all its appurtenances;

in the city of León: the church of the Holy Sepulchre, with all its appurtenances;

at Rivo Sicco: the church of Saint Justus of Paralelos, with all its appurtenances;

at Medina: the church of Saint Peter, with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Lawrence of Oterolo, with all its appurtenances;

in the village of Morel: the church of Saint Pelagius, with its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Justus of Villa Vela, with all its appurtenances;

in the same diocese: the village of Golpigar, with all its appurtenances, and the village of Versadam, [Col. 1283D] with all its appurtenances;

at Mazella: the hospice, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Nava, with its appurtenances; and the church of Saint Peter of Castro Olfereth, with its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Astorga: the church of Saint Peter of Cabaneros, with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Mary of Zohtes, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Saint James: the church of Saint Sebastian of Tavairoas, with its hermitage and other appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Mary of Nogaria, with its appurtenances; and the monastery of Saint Saviour of Sobradel, with all its appurtenances;

in the diocese of Tui: the church of Saint Peter of Nogaria, called [Col. 1284A] Sardoma, with all its appurtenances;

while preserving, of course, the rights and reverence due to the diocesan bishops.

Moreover, we decree that no person whatsoever may seize the aforesaid possessions and goods, retain them when seized, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the complete benefit of you and your successors canonically appointed. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our enactment, rashly attempts to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, fails to make proper amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, acknowledge himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and [Col. 1284B] blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all of you who preserve justice for these things may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Honorius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed.

I, Ubertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed.

I, Rossemannus, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 1284C] Given at Benevento, through the hand of Aimeric, deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of September [4 September], in the sixth indiction, in the year 1128 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

LXXIII. He receives the abbey of Floreffe under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions. (1128, 4 November.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Sacred Order of Prémontré*, vol. I, proofs, p. 52.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Richard, abbot of Saint Mary of Floreffe, and his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

[Col. 1284D] Since without [lacuna] neither the unity of religion nor of charity can subsist, nor can service pleasing to God be offered, it accords with apostolic authority to love religious persons and foster religious places by the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved son Richard in the Lord, assenting to your reasonable petitions, we receive into the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection the monastery of Blessed Mary of Floreffe, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside; and we confirm it by the authority of this document. We decree that whatever churches and possessions that monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in the future, by the Lord’s bounty, acquire through grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors. We decree also that the free [lacuna], granted by the decision of our venerable brother Albero, formerly bishop of Liège, shall be preserved for ever, without prejudice to the right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. You shall receive chrism and oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of clerics from the bishop of Liège, if he enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide them freely and without any exaction. Upon your death, you who are now abbot of that place, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or violence; but the brothers shall provide for the election, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, of the person whom all consent upon, or whom the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel chooses. [Col. 1285B] Moreover, we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain them when seized, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations; but let all be preserved whole for the complete benefit of the uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this document of our enactment, rashly attempts to act against it and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make proper amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, acknowledge himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, [Col. 1285C] be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for that same monastery may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the reward of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Honorius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aimeric, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of November [4 November], in the seventh indiction, in the year 1128 from the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

LXXIV. To Alexander, bishop, and the clergy of Liège.—The supreme pontiff condemns the evil custom of demanding money from those received as canons. (1128, 7 November.)

[D’ACHERY, *Spicilegium*, vol. III, p. 479.]

[Col. 1285D]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Alexander, bishop, and the clergy of Liège: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of your brethren who came to us, we have learned that an abominable custom has long been practised in your Church of Liège: whoever wishes to become a canon there must pay a specified sum of money to the provost and dean. We have also learned that archdeacons and deans do this in connection with the investitures of churches and altars. It is written in the Gospel that our Lord cast those buying and selling out of the temple. Therefore, by these present letters, firmly commanding, we direct that so evil a custom shall in no way henceforth be maintained among you, but shall be utterly abolished. If anyone thereafter presumes to do this, we command that both giver and receiver shall no longer have a place in the Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of November [7 November].

LXXV. He exhorts the clergy, consuls, and people of Pistoia to contribute money to Bishop I[ldeprand] for building a church of Saint Peter. (Between 1125 and 1129, 29 March.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, ed. Luc., IV, 588.]

[Col. 1286B]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the clergy, consuls, and people of Pistoia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our venerable brother I[ldeprand], your bishop, out of love for religion, has, as we have learned, built a certain church in honour of God and blessed Peter near the city of Pistoia, and is said to have established there religious men devoted to divine service. Therefore, so that the vow and religious desire of your pastor and bishop may be fully accomplished, we command your whole community by way of request to provide, from the resources entrusted to you by God, charitable assistance and counsel for the completion of so salutary a work, so that you may share in the sacrifices and prayers [Col. 1286C] which will there be poured out before the divine presence, and may sing with the Prophet: “Lord, I have loved the beauty of thy house, and the place where thy glory dwells”; and may be crowned with the same reward of immortality.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April [29 March].

LXXVI. To Louis VI, king of the Franks.—He receives Henry, the king’s clerical son, into his protection. (Between 1125 and 1128, 31 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 322.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved son in Christ Louis, illustrious and glorious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1286D] The love of inward charity, by which we embrace your person with the affection of paternal tenderness, inclines our ears to grant your petitions. For the love and reverent devotion which you show to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church urge us to attend to your benefit and that of your kingdom. We therefore receive into the protection both of blessed Peter and of ourselves your son Henry, whom you have vowed to devote to divine service. Accordingly, we fortify him, as a special son of the Apostolic See, and the goods which, whether through your royal generosity or by other means under the favour of divine grace, he may acquire, by the authority of our protection. Let no person rashly disturb his person or goods; but let all be preserved quiet and free for him [Col. 1287A] under the patronage of blessed Peter and the Roman Church. If anyone proves a violator of this our confirmation, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be struck by the punishment of the Apostolic See.

Given at the Lateran, on the day before the Kalends of April [31 March].

LXXVII. To Odalric, bishop of Constance.—He admonishes him to urge Count Rudolph of Lenzburg to desist from harassing the monastery of Rheinau. (Between 1125 and 1129, 7 April.)

[HERGOTT, *Genealogia diplomatica augustae gentis Habsburgicae*, Vienna, Austria, 1737, vol. II, p. 142.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Odalric, bishop of Constance: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1287B] Just as cultivators of justice and lovers of religion are to be embraced in the arms of true charity, so plunderers and persecutors of God’s Church are to be restrained by fitting punishments. Therefore we command your diligence carefully to admonish Count Rudolph of Lenzburg, that he desist from the harassment of the monastery of Rheinau and leave it wholly in its ancient and granted liberty. If he scorns to obey your admonitions, administer due justice against him.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of April [7 April].

LXXVIII. To Burchard, bishop of Meaux.—He announces that, with the assent of Theobald, count of Blois, the evil custom of plundering the Church’s goods after the death of bishops has been abolished. (Between 1125 and 1129, 15 April.)

[D. DU PLESSIS, *History of the Church of Meaux*, II, 24.]

[Col. 1287C]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Burchard, bishop of Meaux: greeting and apostolic blessing, etc.

Therefore, by the force of this present document, we abolish the evil practice and iniquitous custom by which, at the death of the bishops of Meaux, the goods of your Church were plundered—a custom annulled by our beloved son, the illustrious man Theobald, count of Blois, and confirmed by the authority of his document. We command absolutely that it shall no longer be maintained in your Church, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May [15 April].

LXXIX. To the parishioners of the church of Saint Frigdian at Lucca. (Between 1125 and 1129, 29 April.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, ed. Luc., IV, 588.]

[Col. 1287D]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the parishioners of blessed Frigdian: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We give thanks to your whole community because, as we have learned from the report of our beloved son A., your prior, you love and honour both him and the brethren there devoted to divine service, and support them from the resources bestowed upon you by God. Therefore we ask and exhort you in the Lord, and enjoin it upon you for the remission of your sins, [Col. 1288A] that you firmly persevere in the good beginning you have made and in no way turn aside from reverence and love for that church.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of May [29 April].

LXXX. Bull confirming the church and goods of Steinfeld. (Between 1125 and 1129, 29 April.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Sacred Order of Prémontré*, vol. II, proofs, ch. 521.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Berwin, provost of the monastery of Saint Mary, situated in the place called Steinfeld, and his brethren professing the canonical life: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1288B] Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with reason, it becomes us gladly to grant it and extend suitable support. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, granting assent to your reasonable petitions, we confirm by the authority of this document your place called Steinfeld, decreeing that whatever goods and possessions it now justly and lawfully possesses, or may in the future, through the Lord’s bounty, acquire by lawful means, shall remain secure and inviolate to you, without prejudice to the right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. We decree also that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolably for ever. Moreover, we decree that no person whatsoever [Col. 1288C] may rashly disturb that place, seize its possessions, retain them when seized, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations. If anyone attempts to act contrary to this our confirmation, let him know without doubt that he will incur the punishment of the Apostolic See, unless he corrects his presumption through worthy satisfaction.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of May [29 April].

LXXXI. To Bernard, count of Melgueil.—He commands that the coinage of Melgueil shall be made nowhere but at Melgueil. (Between 1125 and 1129, 23 May.)

[D. BOUQUET, vol. XV, p. 265.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1288D] son Bernard, illustrious count of Melgueil: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Church defends what is beyond reproach. We wish to uphold and assist you as a special son of blessed Peter, and by apostolic authority we command that the coinage of Melgueil be minted at Melgueil alone. It therefore concerns you, if you desire to possess our protection, to introduce no falsity into the making of the coinage and henceforth not have it minted otherwise than was established in the time of Calixtus.

Given in the territory of Colonna, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May], in the third year of our pontificate. [Note: “[Col. 1287] The words ‘in the third year of our pontificate,’ etc., were added by another hand. JAFFÉ.”]

LXXXII. He receives under the protection of the Apostolic See the hospital house and church of Saint Mary in the diocese of Ceneda. (Between 1125 and 1129, 28 November.)

[CORNELIUS, *Churches of Venice*, 1749, quarto, X, III, 29.]

[Col. 1289A]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Rainer, provost, and his brethren, both present and future, for ever.

It is fitting readily to grant consent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Accordingly, beloved sons in Christ, we graciously admit your petitions; and we receive into the right and ownership of blessed Peter, and strengthen by the authority of the Apostolic See, the hospital built in the territory of Ceneda, in the place called [Col. 1289B] Talpone, with all its dependencies, and the house there constructed in honour of blessed Mary ever virgin in order that it might become a church—both of which you have bestowed upon the holy Roman Church by a charter of offering. We decree that whatever goods that hospital now justly possesses, or may in the future, through the Lord’s bounty, acquire by lawful means, shall remain secure and inviolate to it. As a token of the protection of that hospital, however, we establish this annual payment to be made by it: each year it shall pay to the Lateran Palace two pounds, one of incense and the other of wax. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1289C] person, knowing this document of our enactment, rashly attempts to act against it and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make proper amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of rank and office, acknowledge himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for that same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of December [28 November].

LXXXIII. To A[dalbero], archbishop of Hamburg.—He commends E., cardinal priest. (Between 1126 and 1129, 23 May.)

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburg Documents*, I, 130.]

[Col. 1289D]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., archbishop of Bremen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since no one can render service pleasing to God without peace and tranquillity of mind, and so that the controversy being conducted between you and our brother A., archbishop of London, may, by the Lord’s haste, be brought to its due conclusion, we have thought fit to send our beloved son E., cardinal priest, from our side into your regions. [Col. 1290A] We have committed to him the careful investigation and examination of the matter itself. Therefore we command you graciously to receive him and, at the place and time at which you are summoned by him, to come into his presence in order to discuss the aforesaid matter.

Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May].

LXXXIV. To the archdeacon and precentor of Agde. (Between 1126 and 1129, 31 May.)

[GARIEL, *Series of the Prelates of Maguelonne*, p. 142.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the archdeacon and precentor of Agde: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1290B] Our brother, the bishop of Maguelonne, has informed us that the abbot of Aniane, in his diocese and subject to his jurisdiction, refuses to attend his synods, to the prejudice and burden of both the bishop and his Church. Therefore, by apostolic letters, we command your discretion that, after summoning the parties and hearing what they judge should be put forward, you shall determine, without regard to appeal, whatever is canonical, causing what you decide to be firmly observed through ecclesiastical censure.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of June [31 May], in the fifth year of our pontificate. [Note: “[Col. 1289] ‘In the fifth year of our pontificate’ has been added conjecturally. JAFFÉ.”]

LXXXV. To the clergy and people of Toul.—He commands observance of the sentence of excommunication pronounced against Theodoric of Imbercurte. (Between 1127 and 1129, 17 March.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, vol. XV, p. 266.]

[Col. 1290C]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clergy and people established throughout the parish of Toul: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Theodoric of Imbercurte, having come to the Apostolic See, complained that he had been unjustly excommunicated by our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Toul, while appealing to a Roman hearing. On the other hand, the archdeacons of Toul—Hugh of Gundricourt, Hugh the White, and the priest Olderic—asserted that they had long before pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him because he had violently seized the castle of Commercy from the Church of Toul. [Col. 1290D] They began to affirm in our presence that the authority and licence to excommunicate plunderers of their property had been granted to them by Richinus, bishop of Toul, and subsequently confirmed in writing by our predecessor Pope Calixtus II of blessed memory. To make us more certain, they produced the authenticated documents in evidence. Therefore, having heard and examined the arguments of both sides and taken counsel with our brethren the bishops and cardinals, we did not absolve Theodoric, since, long before he appealed to a Roman hearing, he had been excommunicated [Col. 1291A] by canons who were permitted to do so by apostolic grant. We therefore command your whole community to abstain from him as from one excommunicated, until he makes satisfaction to the Church of Toul.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April [17 March].

LXXXVI. To William, archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See. (Between 1127 and 1129, 19 April.)

[WARTHON, *Anglia Sacra*, II, 674.]

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren William, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, and all bishops established throughout England: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1291B] Our brother Urban, bishop of Llandaff, coming before the clemency of the Apostolic See, declared that in the assembly and before your presence he had lodged a complaint against Bishops Bernard of St Davids and Richard of Hereford concerning a portion of his episcopal diocese held by them. But those brethren, without making any reply to his complaint, inverted the proper order and began to attack him on other matters. That this is contrary both to the ordinances of the sacred canons and to legal enactments is beyond doubt. For in a judicial proceeding and the examination of a single case, the defendant cannot become plaintiff except by way of an exception. He, however, requesting observance of judicial order—that a reasonable answer first be made to the charges he had brought—appealed to your discretion, brother archbishop, since you were sitting as judge. Because he could not obtain what he sought, feeling that a grave injury was being inflicted upon him, he appealed to the Roman hearing, the common remedy of the oppressed, and summoned the aforesaid Bishops Bernard and Richard to answer his complaints in our presence during the middle of Lent.

But he himself remained with us for some time; the summoned parties, when the appointed date arrived, neither came nor sent representatives. Therefore, after common deliberation with our brethren, both bishops and cardinals, and having heard on this matter the testimony of two witnesses, we have invested him with the district concerning which the complaint had been made—namely Herigin, Hstratewi, Goher, Cadweli, and Cantrebocan—[Col. 1291D] without prejudice to the rights of the churches of Hereford and St Davids. We have set the coming Lent as the term both for Urban of Llandaff and for Bishops Bernard and Richard; then, when each party has set forth in our presence the grounds of its complaints, it shall obtain what the rule of justice prescribes. Meanwhile, we command that Brother Urban hold the district which was in dispute wholly, peacefully, and without anyone’s opposition. Therefore, brother archbishop, do not permit the aforesaid Bishops Bernard and Richard in any way, whether personally or through their officials, to occupy or invade that district.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May.

LXXXVII. Confirms the regular canons established in the monastery of Agaunum. (Between 1128 and 1129, November 7.)

[Gallia Christiana, XII, documents, 430.]

[Col. 1292A]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons of the church of St Maurice the martyr at Agaunum: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Apostolic teaching and the venerable authority of the saints exhort us, if we truly wish to please God, to strive to live religiously. For who has been able to please God without purity of religion? Or who has ascended to contemplation of the Godhead except with a chaste and clean heart? Therefore we, though unworthy, who sit in the chair of Blessed Peter, desire, through the administration of his Church entrusted to us by God, both to establish religious observance and to strengthen the stability of the Apostolic See by its power.

It therefore pleases us that, as we have learned by inspection of your letters, you have unanimously decreed, through divine inspiration, to establish regular canons in your church and always to appoint religious men in the place of those who die. Praising your pious desires and reasonable purpose, we command and, by the authority of Blessed Peter and our own, confirm that regular canons shall henceforth serve God there and that the canonical order shall be inviolably preserved there in future times. We establish that, once there is a sufficient number of regular men in the aforesaid church, a religious and wise abbot shall be appointed there, one who knows how worthily to preside over the sacred community in learning and conduct, and who shall be chosen after divine grace has been invoked.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of November.

LXXXVIII. To Matthew, bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See.—Entrusts to him for adjudication the dispute between Henry, bishop of Verdun, assailed by many accusations, and his accusers. (Year 1129.)

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, vol. XV, p. 269.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother MATTHEW, bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As your brotherhood knows, the canons of Verdun, formerly appearing before us, accused their bishop Henry of squandering the property and treasury of the Church, and of simony. Since we could not pass over so grave an offence in silence, we set a date for each party; and they appeared before us on the day appointed. At length the accusers, through their advocate, first made certain statements concerning the bishop’s election and the incontinence of his life; then, having entered a formal accusation of simony and of squandering the Church’s goods and treasury, they accused the bishop in person.

The other party, which had come with the bishop, sought to exclude one of those accusers by a written accusation that he had kept a concubine while in the diaconate. Conversely, those who had come with the accusers sought to exclude this man from the accusation by imputing to him the crime of perjury. Since they were breaking out all too unreasonably into insulting language, lest through so many rejoinders by the accusers the case should be prolonged without end:

> [Note: [Col. 1293D] Laurence of Liège repeated these same words in his commentaries, adding: “Honorius asked the venerable Laurence, abbot of St Vitonus, who too was present: ‘Father, what do you say about the charges brought against the bishop?’ And he replied: ‘Lord, I did not see them, but the people cry out.’ The pope seized upon the words from his mouth; and, because the cardinals favoured the bishop and the litigation allowed no certain conclusion, he could determine no judgment, and he entrusted the case for examination to Matthew, bishop of Albano, his legate in Gaul.” Moreover, what Matthew did in this case at Châlons was committed to writing by the same Laurence of Liège.]

we entrusted the case to the tested judgment of your brotherhood for settlement. You, therefore, having summoned both the aforesaid bishop and the opposing party before you, are to proceed to Châlons; there, after calling to your aid the archbishop of Trier, other bishops, and also wise and religious men, you are to hear the case carefully and investigate it by diligent inquiry. If suitable accusers and witnesses appear, define the case canonically after taking counsel with the brethren. Otherwise, before the Church whose face he has injured, let him clearly demonstrate his innocence in accordance with your counsel and that of the other brethren who will be with you; afterward, settle peace between them concerning their complaints, whether through justice or agreement.

LXXXIX. Privilege for the church of St Peter at Bologna. (Year 1129, March 15.)

[Savioli, *Annali Bolognesi*, Appendix, I, II, p. 174.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons LAMBERT, archpriest, and the other canons of the church of Blessed Peter at Bologna, present and future: greeting.

Whenever a request is made of us which we recognize to concern us closely, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and extend the desired assistance. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your reasonable petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and under our own protection the Bolognese church of Blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the page of this our writing.

We establish for you whatever goods you justly possess or ought to possess, whether lands and vineyards or various kinds of holdings situated in individual places and territories, which are known to have come to you by whatever means or title and through whomever, or which you may acquire hereafter. Moreover, we make subject to you all tithes of the entire parish of St Mary called *de Buida*, and the church of St Mary situated on Mount Palense, with its offerings and all its appurtenances, and whatever shall there be offered by those who fear God for the salvation of living and dead. Also the olive groves in the territory called *de Garda*, and the house near the bishop’s palace belonging to that same church. All houses everywhere belonging to the same canonical right, or whatever you now possess by right of that same church, or which you or your successors may hereafter justly acquire. Also the whole demesne of that church; the church of St John the Baptist situated [Col. 1294A] beside the greater church; one half of all the tithes of the entire parish of St Peter called *in Barbarorum*; and we likewise grant you all movable property which may rightly be said and named to belong to you in any way.

By this page of our decree and grant, we provide that you may securely hold and possess these things quietly and peacefully, all contradiction or molestation by any person being removed. Therefore we decree that no archbishop, bishop, duke, marquis, count, viscount, nor any great or small person of whatever rank shall presume to hold a court concerning your property or possessions, to inflict injury upon those dwelling on your lands, to coerce or harass them, to take a pledge from them, or to flog them. Rather, it shall be lawful for you and all your successors at all times to enjoy all your goods and possessions in peace under the protection of our guardianship, free from disturbance by every temporal power.

If any rash person attempts to act against this decree of our confirmation, presumes to inflict any molestation, or fails to observe the foregoing, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes fitting amends by adequate satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the aforesaid Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Honorius, bishop of the catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Aimeric, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1129 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Honorius II.

XC. Bull for the monastery of Vendôme. (Year 1129, March 24.)

[Mabillon, *Annales Benedictini*, VI, 653, from the original.]

HONORIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved son GEOFFREY, abbot of the monastery of Vendôme, and to his successors to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The most holy Roman Church, which retains the primacy over all Churches granted to it by God, ought, like a diligent mother, to provide for each Church with constant watchfulness. It is therefore just and reasonable that churches and venerable places, especially those which belong to the special right and possession of the holy Roman Church, which by God’s ordinance we serve, should receive the honour of a more special prerogative and be strengthened by the protection of apostolic authority.

Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Geoffrey, we have judged that your reasonable petitions ought not without cause to be granted: namely, that we should fortify with a privilege of the Apostolic See the monastery of Vendôme over which, by God’s ordinance, you preside, a monastery offered to the Apostolic See by its very founders, Geoffrey, count of Anjou, and Agnes, countess of Poitiers, following the example of our predecessors of holy memory, the Roman pontiffs Alexander, Urban, Paschal, and Calixtus.

Therefore let the possessions and goods which that monastery now justly and canonically possesses remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. We have thought fit to record by their proper names the following: the church [Col. 1295B] of St Mary of Sougères; the church of St Mary in the castle of Oléron; the church of St Nicholas; the church of St Mary of Castels; the church of St Clement of Crédon; the church of St Saviour beside the walls of Angers; and the chapel of St Eutropius.
